docs.title: file-utils Documentation
docs.text: A Python package for streaming file operations with support for CSV, TSV, JSONL, XML, Avro, Arrow IPC, and Parquet formats. Includes uniform local, S3, and HTTP/HTTPS file access.

docs.title: Quick Navigation
docs.text:
• Installation
  • Quick Start
  • File Formats
  • API Reference
  • Examples

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Streaming file operations - Process large files without loading them entirely into memory
  • Multiple storage backends - Local filesystem, S3, HTTP/HTTPS
  • Format conversion - Convert between CSV, TSV, JSONL, XML, Avro, Arrow IPC, and Parquet
  • Efficient I/O - Use fsspec for unified file access across different storage systems
  • Chunked processing - Read and write files in chunks for memory efficiency

  • S3 - Amazon S3 and compatible services (MinIO, etc.)

docs.title: is_s3(path)
docs.text:
Check if a path is an S3 URL.

Parameters: - path (str | Path): Path to check

Returns: - bool: True if the path is an S3 URL (s3://, s3a://, s3n://)

Example: 

from file_utils import is_s3

is_s3("s3://bucket/key")  # True
is_s3("/local/path")  # False

docs.title: split_s3(path)
docs.text:
Split an S3 URL into bucket and key.

Parameters: - path (str | Path): S3 URL

Returns: - tuple[str, str]: (bucket, key)

Raises: - ValueError: If not an S3 URL or bucket is empty

Example: 

from file_utils import split_s3

bucket, key = split_s3("s3://my-bucket/data/file.csv")
# bucket = "my-bucket", key = "data/file.csv"

docs.title: open_any(path, mode='rb', **kwargs)
docs.text:
Open a file from any storage backend (local, S3, HTTP/HTTPS).

Parameters: - path (str | Path): File path or URL - mode (str): File mode ('rb', 'wb', 'rt', 'wt', etc.) - **kwargs: Additional arguments passed to fsspec.open

Returns: - File-like object

Example: 

from file_utils import open_any

# Open local file
with open_any("/path/to/file.csv", "rb") as f:
    data = f.read()

# Open S3 file
with open_any("s3://bucket/key", "rb") as f:
    data = f.read()

# Open HTTP file
with open_any("https://example.com/file.csv", "rb") as f:
    data = f.read()

docs.title: exists(path)
docs.text:
Check if a path exists.

Parameters: - path (str | Path): File path or URL

Returns: - bool: True if the path exists

Example: 

from file_utils import exists

exists("/local/file.csv")  # True/False

docs.title: file_size(path)
docs.text:
Get the size of a file in bytes.

Parameters: - path (str | Path): File path or URL

Returns: - int: Size in bytes

Example: 

from file_utils import file_size

size = file_size("s3://bucket/large-file.parquet")
print(f"File size: {size} bytes")

docs.title: download(src, dst, **kwargs)
docs.text:
Download a file from any source to a local destination.

Parameters: - src (str | Path): Source path or URL (local, s3://, http://, https://) - dst (str | Path): Destination local path - **kwargs: Additional arguments passed to underlying download functions

Returns: - str | Path: The destination path

Example: 

from file_utils import download

# Download from HTTPS
download("https://example.com/file.csv", "/local/file.csv")

# Download from S3
download("s3://bucket/key", "/local/key")

# Copy local file
download("/source/file.csv", "/dest/file.csv")

docs.title: s3_client(endpoint_url=None, region=None, **kwargs)
docs.text:
Create an S3 client with configurable endpoint and region.

Parameters: - endpoint_url (str | None): S3 endpoint URL - region (str | None): AWS region - **kwargs: Additional arguments passed to boto3.client

Returns: - boto3.client: S3 client

Example: 

from file_utils import s3_client

# Create client with default configuration
client = s3_client()

# Create client with custom endpoint (e.g., MinIO)
client = s3_client(
    endpoint_url="https://minio.example.com:9000",
    region="us-east-1"
)

docs.title: upload(src, s3_url, client=None, *, threshold_mb=64, chunk_mb=64, max_concurrency=8, extra_args=None)
docs.text:
Upload a file to S3 with multipart support.

Parameters: - src (str): Source path (local or s3://) - s3_url (str): Destination S3 URL - client (boto3.client | None): Optional S3 client - threshold_mb (int): Minimum file size in MB for multipart upload (default: 64) - chunk_mb (int): Chunk size in MB for multipart upload (default: 64) - max_concurrency (int): Maximum number of concurrent uploads (default: 8) - extra_args (dict | None): Extra arguments passed to upload_fileobj

Returns: - str: The S3 URL

Raises: - ValueError: If s3_url is not a valid S3 URL

Example: 

from file_utils import upload

# Upload local file to S3
upload("/local/file.csv", "s3://bucket/data/file.csv")

# Upload with custom settings
upload(
    "/local/large-file.parquet",
    "s3://bucket/data/large-file.parquet",
    threshold_mb=128,
    chunk_mb=32,
    max_concurrency=4
)

docs.title: s3_download(s3_url, dst, client=None, *, threshold_mb=64, chunk_mb=64, max_concurrency=8)
docs.text:
Download a file from S3 (legacy function, use download() for general use).

Parameters: - s3_url (str): Source S3 URL - dst (str): Destination path - client (boto3.client | None): Optional S3 client - threshold_mb (int): Minimum file size in MB for multipart download (default: 64) - chunk_mb (int): Chunk size in MB for multipart download (default: 64) - max_concurrency (int): Maximum number of concurrent downloads (default: 8)

Returns: - str: The destination path

Raises: - ValueError: If s3_url is not a valid S3 URL

Example: 

from file_utils import s3_download

s3_download("s3://bucket/data/file.csv", "/local/file.csv")

docs.title: list_keys(s3_url, client=None)
docs.text:
List keys under a prefix in S3.

Parameters: - s3_url (str): S3 URL with optional prefix - client (boto3.client | None): Optional S3 client

Yields: - str: Key names

Raises: - ValueError: If s3_url is not a valid S3 URL

Example: 

from file_utils import list_keys

# List all keys in a bucket
for key in list_keys("s3://bucket/"):
    print(key)

# List keys with a prefix
for key in list_keys("s3://bucket/data/"):
    print(key)

docs.title: detect_format(path)
docs.text:
Detect format from file extension.

Parameters: - path (str | Path): File path or URL

Returns: - str: Format name ('csv', 'jsonl', 'xml', 'avro', 'parquet', 'arrow')

Raises: - ValueError: If extension is unknown

Example: 

from file_utils import detect_format

format = detect_format("data.csv")
# Returns: "csv"

docs.title: convert(src, dst, **kwargs)
docs.text:
Generic conversion function that automatically detects source and destination formats.

Parameters: - src (str | Path): Source file path or URL - dst (str | Path): Destination file path - **kwargs: Format-specific options

Example:

docs.title: Configure S3 client
docs.text:
import os
from file_utils import s3_client

# Option 1: Use environment variables
os.environ["AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID"] = "your-access-key"
os.environ["AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY"] = "your-secret-key"
os.environ["AWS_DEFAULT_REGION"] = "us-east-1"

client = s3_client()

# Option 2: Custom endpoint (e.g., MinIO)
client = s3_client(
    endpoint_url="https://minio.example.com:9000",
    region="us-east-1"
)

# Option 3: Pass client to operations
from file_utils import upload

upload("/local/file.csv", "s3://bucket/file.csv", client=client)

docs.title: List S3 objects

from file_utils import list_keys

# List all objects in a bucket
for key in list_keys("s3://my-bucket/"):
    print(key)

# List objects with a prefix
for key in list_keys("s3://my-bucket/data/2024/"):
    print(key)

docs.title: Batch conversion
docs.text:
from file_utils import csv_to_parquet, detect_format
import os

input_dir = "/path/to/input"
output_dir = "/path/to/output"

for filename in os.listdir(input_dir):
    input_path = os.path.join(input_dir, filename)
    output_path = os.path.join(output_dir, f"{os.path.splitext(filename)[0]}.parquet")

    fmt = detect_format(input_path)

    if fmt == "csv":
        csv_to_parquet(input_path, output_path)
    elif fmt == "jsonl":
        from file_utils import jsonl_to_parquet
        jsonl_to_parquet(input_path, output_path)

docs.title: Stream and convert

from file_utils import open_any, csv_to_parquet
import tempfile
import os

# For very large files, use temporary files
def stream_and_convert(s3_path, output_path):
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
        # Download to temp
        temp_csv = os.path.join(tmpdir, "temp.csv")
        download(s3_path, temp_csv)

        # Convert
        csv_to_parquet(temp_csv, output_path)

        # Cleanup happens automatically

stream_and_convert("s3://my-bucket/huge.csv", "/local/huge.parquet")

docs.title: Process all files in S3 bucket
docs.text:
from file_utils import list_keys, download, csv_to_parquet, detect_format
import os

bucket = "my-bucket"
prefix = "data/2024/01/"
output_dir = "/local/output"

for key in list_keys(f"s3://{bucket}/{prefix}"):
    # Download file
    local_path = os.path.join(output_dir, os.path.basename(key))
    download(f"s3://{bucket}/{key}", local_path)

    # Convert based on format
    fmt = detect_format(local_path)

    if fmt == "csv":
        output_path = os.path.join(output_dir, f"{os.path.splitext(key)[0]}.parquet")
        csv_to_parquet(local_path, output_path)

docs.title: Handle missing files
docs.text:
from file_utils import exists, open_any, download

# Check before opening
if exists("s3://my-bucket/data.csv"):
    with open_any("s3://my-bucket/data.csv", "rt") as f:
        data = f.read()
else:
    print("File does not exist!")

# Or use try-except
try:
    with open_any("s3://my-bucket/data.csv", "rt") as f:
        data = f.read()
except FileNotFoundError:
    print("File not found!")

docs.title: Retry logic for downloads
docs.text:
from file_utils import download
import time

max_retries = 3
retry_delay = 5  # seconds

for attempt in range(max_retries):
    try:
        download("https://example.com/data/file.csv", "/local/file.csv")
        break
    except Exception as e:
        if attempt == max_retries - 1:
            raise
        print(f"Attempt {attempt + 1} failed: {e}")
        time.sleep(retry_delay)

docs.title: Example 1: ETL Pipeline
docs.text:
from file_utils import (
    download,
    list_keys,
    csv_to_parquet,
    jsonl_to_parquet,
    detect_format
)
import os

def etl_from_s3_to_parquet(bucket, prefix, output_dir):
    """Download files from S3, convert to Parquet, and save locally."""

    for key in list_keys(f"s3://{bucket}/{prefix}"):
        # Download file
        local_file = os.path.join(output_dir, os.path.basename(key))
        download(f"s3://{bucket}/{key}", local_file)

        # Convert based on format
        fmt = detect_format(local_file)
        output_file = os.path.join(
            output_dir,
            f"{os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(key))[0]}.parquet"
        )

        if fmt == "csv":
            csv_to_parquet(local_file, output_file)
        elif fmt == "jsonl":
            jsonl_to_parquet(local_file, output_file)

        # Cleanup
        os.remove(local_file)

# Run ETL
etl_from_s3_to_parquet("my-bucket", "raw-data/", "/local/processed")

docs.title: Example 2: Data Lake Ingestion
docs.text:
from file_utils import (
    list_keys,
    download,
    xml_to_parquet,
    csv_to_parquet,
    jsonl_to_parquet
)
import os
from datetime import datetime

def ingest_data_lake(source_dir, target_bucket):
    """Ingest files from local directory to S3 data lake in Parquet format."""

    date = datetime.now().strftime("%Y/%m/%d")

    for filename in os.listdir(source_dir):
        input_path = os.path.join(source_dir, filename)

        # Create output path
        output_filename = f"{os.path.splitext(filename)[0]}.parquet"
        output_path = f"s3://{target_bucket}/data/{date}/{output_filename}"

        # Convert based on extension
        if filename.endswith(".xml"):
            xml_to_parquet(input_path, output_path)
        elif filename.endswith(".csv"):
            csv_to_parquet(input_path, output_path)
        elif filename.endswith(".jsonl"):
            jsonl_to_parquet(input_path, output_path)

# Run ingestion
ingest_data_lake("/local/raw-data", "my-data-lake")

docs.title: Example 3: Web Scraping and Storage
docs.text:
from file_utils import download, jsonl_to_parquet
import tempfile
import os

def scrape_and_store(urls, output_dir):
    """Download files from URLs and store as Parquet."""

    for url in urls:
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
            # Download file
            filename = os.path.basename(url.split("?")[0])
            local_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, filename)
            download(url, local_path)

            # Convert to Parquet
            output_path = os.path.join(
                output_dir,
                f"{os.path.splitext(filename)[0]}.parquet"
            )

            if filename.endswith(".jsonl"):
                jsonl_to_parquet(local_path, output_path)
            elif filename.endswith(".csv"):
                from file_utils import csv_to_parquet
                csv_to_parquet(local_path, output_path)

# Run scraping
urls = [
    "https://example.com/data/file1.jsonl",
    "https://example.com/data/file2.csv",
]
scrape_and_store(urls, "/local/scraped-data")

docs.title: Supported File Formats
docs.text: file-utils supports the following file formats with streaming read/write and conversion capabilities:

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: CSV is a simple, widely-used format for tabular data. Each line represents a row, and columns are separated by commas (or other delimiters).

docs.title: Supported Features
docs.text:
• ✅ Reading and writing
  • ✅ Custom delimiters (including TSV with tab delimiter)
  • ✅ Conversion to/from other formats
  • ✅ Chunked reading for large files

docs.title: Usage Examples
docs.text:
from file_utils import open_any, csv_to_parquet

# Read CSV
with open_any("data.csv", "rt") as f:
    for line in f:
        print(line)

# Convert CSV to Parquet
csv_to_parquet("input.csv", "output.parquet")

# Read CSV in chunks
with open_any("large.csv", "rb") as f:
    while chunk := f.read(1024 * 1024):  # 1MB chunks
        process(chunk)

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• First row is treated as header by default
  • Supports custom delimiters (comma, tab, semicolon, etc.)
  • Automatic type inference

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: TSV is similar to CSV but uses tabs as delimiters. Often used in data exchange where comma characters might appear in the data.

docs.title: Supported Features
docs.text:
• ✅ Reading and writing (handled as CSV with tab delimiter)
  • ✅ Conversion to/from other formats
  • ✅ Chunked reading for large files

docs.title: Usage Examples
docs.text:
from file_utils import tsv_to_parquet, parquet_to_csv

# Convert TSV to Parquet
tsv_to_parquet("input.tsv", "output.parquet")

# Convert Parquet to TSV (with tab delimiter)
parquet_to_csv("input.parquet", "output.tsv", delimiter="\t")

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: JSONL is a format where each line is a valid JSON object. Also known as NDJSON (Newline-Delimited JSON). Ideal for streaming and incremental processing.

docs.title: Supported Features
docs.text:
• ✅ Reading and writing
  • ✅ Conversion to/from other formats
  • ✅ Streaming line-by-line
  • ✅ Handling of large files

docs.title: Usage Examples
docs.text:
from file_utils import open_any, jsonl_to_parquet, parquet_to_jsonl

# Read JSONL line by line
with open_any("data.jsonl", "rt") as f:
    for line in f:
        record = json.loads(line)
        process(record)

# Convert JSONL to Parquet
jsonl_to_parquet("input.jsonl", "output.parquet")

# Convert Parquet to JSONL
parquet_to_jsonl("input.parquet", "output.jsonl")

docs.title: File Extensions
docs.text:
• .jsonl (preferred)
  • .ndjson
  • .json (treated as JSONL in this context)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: XML (eXtensible Markup Language) is a markup language that defines a set of rules for encoding documents in a format that is both human-readable and machine-readable.

docs.title: Supported Features
docs.text:
• ✅ Reading and writing
  • ✅ Conversion to/from CSV, JSONL, Parquet
  • ✅ Streaming XML parsing
  • ✅ Handling of nested structures

docs.title: Usage Examples
docs.text:
from file_utils import open_any, xml_to_csv, xml_to_parquet, csv_to_xml

# Read XML
with open_any("data.xml", "rb") as f:
    content = f.read()

# Convert XML to CSV
xml_to_csv("input.xml", "output.csv")

# Convert XML to Parquet
xml_to_parquet("input.xml", "output.parquet")

# Convert CSV to XML
csv_to_xml("input.csv", "output.xml")

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Uses secure XML parsing (defusedxml) to prevent XML attacks
  • Handles nested XML structures by flattening or creating hierarchical data
  • Supports XML namespaces

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Avro is a binary serialization format developed within Apache's Hadoop project. It uses JSON for defining data types and protocols, and serializes data in a compact binary format.

docs.title: Supported Features
docs.text:
• ✅ Reading and writing
  • ✅ Conversion to/from other formats
  • ✅ Schema preservation
  • ✅ Efficient binary format

docs.title: Usage Examples
docs.text:
from file_utils import open_any, avro_to_parquet, parquet_to_avro

# Read Avro file
with open_any("data.avro", "rb") as f:
    content = f.read()

# Convert Avro to Parquet
avro_to_parquet("input.avro", "output.parquet")

# Convert Parquet to Avro
parquet_to_avro("input.parquet", "output.avro")

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Uses fastavro library for efficient Avro operations
  • Preserves schema information during conversion
  • Binary format (not human-readable)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Arrow IPC is a memory format for representing Arrow data in a language-agnostic way. It enables efficient data exchange between processes and systems without serialization overhead.

docs.title: Supported Features
docs.text:
• ✅ Reading and writing
  • ✅ Conversion to/from other formats
  • ✅ Zero-copy operations when possible
  • ✅ Efficient in-memory format

docs.title: Usage Examples
docs.text:
from file_utils import open_any, arrow_to_parquet, parquet_to_arrow

# Read Arrow IPC file
with open_any("data.arrow", "rb") as f:
    content = f.read()

# Convert Arrow to Parquet
arrow_to_parquet("input.arrow", "output.parquet")

# Convert Parquet to Arrow
parquet_to_arrow("input.parquet", "output.arrow")

docs.title: File Extensions
docs.text:
• .arrow
  • .ipc
  • .feather (Apache Arrow's Feather format)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Parquet is a columnar storage file format optimized for use with big data processing frameworks. It provides efficient columnar storage with compression and encoding schemes.

docs.title: Supported Features
docs.text:
• ✅ Reading and writing
  • ✅ Conversion to/from all other formats
  • ✅ Columnar storage
  • ✅ Compression support (zstd, snappy, gzip)
  • ✅ Predicate pushdown
  • ✅ Efficient for analytics

docs.title: Usage Examples
docs.text:
from file_utils import (
    open_any,
    csv_to_parquet,
    jsonl_to_parquet,
    xml_to_parquet,
    avro_to_parquet,
    arrow_to_parquet,
    parquet_to_csv,
    parquet_to_jsonl,
    parquet_to_xml,
    parquet_to_avro,
    parquet_to_arrow
)

# Read Parquet file
with open_any("data.parquet", "rb") as f:
    # Use pyarrow to read
    import pyarrow.parquet as pq
    table = pq.read_table(f)

# Convert CSV to Parquet
csv_to_parquet("input.csv", "output.parquet")

# Convert JSONL to Parquet
jsonl_to_parquet("input.jsonl", "output.parquet")

# Convert Parquet to CSV
parquet_to_csv("input.parquet", "output.csv")

# Convert Parquet to JSONL
parquet_to_jsonl("input.parquet", "output.jsonl")

docs.title: File Extensions
docs.text:
• .parquet
  • .pq (short form)

docs.title: Compression Options
docs.text:
• zstd (default) - Good compression with fast read/write
  • snappy - Very fast compression/decompression
  • gzip - Higher compression ratio, slower
  • brotli - High compression ratio
  • lz4 - Fast compression

docs.title: Format Detection
docs.text:
The detect_format function automatically identifies the file format based on the file extension:

from file_utils import detect_format

formats = [
    "data.csv",
    "data.tsv", 
    "data.jsonl",
    "data.ndjson",
    "data.json",
    "data.xml",
    "data.avro",
    "data.arrow",
    "data.ipc",
    "data.feather",
    "data.parquet",
    "data.pq"
]

for path in formats:
    fmt = detect_format(path)
    print(f"{path} -> {fmt}")

Output: 

data.csv -> csv
data.tsv -> csv
data.jsonl -> jsonl
data.ndjson -> jsonl
data.json -> jsonl
data.xml -> xml
data.avro -> avro
data.arrow -> arrow
data.ipc -> arrow
data.feather -> arrow
data.parquet -> parquet
data.pq -> parquet

docs.text:
• Python 3.8 or higher
  • pip or uv (recommended)

docs.title: Install with uv (Recommended)

# Create a new project
uv init

# Add file-utils as a dependency
uv add git+https://github.com/PVDL23/file-utils.git

# Or if you have the package locally
uv add /path/to/file-utils

pip install /path/to/file-utils

git clone https://github.com/PVDL23/file-utils.git
cd file-utils
pip install .

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
The package requires the following dependencies:

  • pyarrow - For Parquet, Arrow IPC, CSV, and TSV operations
  • fastavro - For Avro format support
  • boto3 - For S3 operations
  • fsspec - For unified file system access (local, S3, HTTP/HTTPS)
  • defusedxml - For secure XML parsing

All dependencies are automatically installed when you install file-utils.

docs.title: Running Tests
docs.text:
The package uses pytest for testing. With uv:

# Run all tests
uv run pytest

uv run pytest -v

uv run pytest tests/test_io.py

# Run with coverage
uv run pytest --cov=src/file_utils --cov-report=term-missing

With pip:

# Run all tests
pytest

# Run tests with verbose output
pytest -v

# Run specific test file
pytest tests/test_io.py

# Run with coverage
pytest --cov=src/file_utils --cov-report=term-missing

docs.title: S3 Configuration
docs.text:
For S3 operations, configure your AWS credentials:

# Set environment variables
export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=your_access_key
export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=your_secret_key
export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=your_region

# Optional: Custom S3 endpoint (e.g., for MinIO)
export S3_ENDPOINT=https://your-minio-server:9000

Or use the s3_client function with explicit parameters:

from file_utils import s3_client

client = s3_client(
    endpoint_url="https://your-minio-server:9000",
    region="us-east-1"
)

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text: Get started with file-utils in just a few minutes!

docs.title: Install the package
docs.text:
uv add /path/to/file-utils
# or
pip install /path/to/file-utils

docs.title: Import the package
docs.text: import file_utils

docs.title: Opening Files
docs.text:
The open_any function provides a unified way to open files from any storage backend:

from file_utils import open_any

# Open a local file
with open_any("/path/to/file.csv", "rb") as f:
    data = f.read()

# Open an S3 file
with open_any("s3://my-bucket/data/file.csv", "rb") as f:
    data = f.read()

# Open from HTTP/HTTPS
with open_any("https://example.com/data/file.csv", "rb") as f:
    data = f.read()

docs.title: Downloading Files
docs.text:
Use the download function to download files from any source to a local destination:

from file_utils import download

# Download from HTTP/HTTPS
download("https://example.com/data/file.csv", "/local/path/file.csv")

# Download from S3
download("s3://my-bucket/data/file.csv", "/local/path/file.csv")

# Copy local file
download("/source/path/file.csv", "/dest/path/file.csv")

docs.title: Check if a file exists
docs.text:
from file_utils import exists

if exists("s3://my-bucket/data/file.csv"):
    print("File exists!")

docs.title: Get file size
docs.text:
from file_utils import file_size

size = file_size("s3://my-bucket/data/file.parquet")
print(f"File size: {size} bytes")

docs.title: Upload a file to S3
docs.text:
from file_utils import upload

upload("/local/path/file.csv", "s3://my-bucket/data/file.csv")

docs.title: Download from S3 (legacy function)
docs.text:
from file_utils import s3_download

s3_download("s3://my-bucket/data/file.csv", "/local/path/file.csv")

docs.title: List keys in S3
docs.text:
from file_utils import list_keys

for key in list_keys("s3://my-bucket/data/"):
    print(key)

docs.title: Delete an S3 object
docs.text:
from file_utils import delete

delete("s3://my-bucket/data/old-file.csv")

docs.title: Format Conversion
docs.text:
Convert between different file formats:

from file_utils import csv_to_parquet, jsonl_to_parquet, xml_to_csv

# Convert CSV to Parquet
csv_to_parquet("/path/to/input.csv", "/path/to/output.parquet")

# Convert JSONL to Parquet
jsonl_to_parquet("/path/to/input.jsonl", "/path/to/output.parquet")

# Convert XML to CSV
xml_to_csv("/path/to/input.xml", "/path/to/output.csv")

docs.title: Detect File Format
docs.text:
from file_utils import detect_format

format = detect_format("/path/to/file.csv")
print(f"Format: {format}")  # Output: csv

docs.title: Working with S3 Client
docs.text:
from file_utils import s3_client

# Create a client with custom endpoint (e.g., MinIO)
client = s3_client(
    endpoint_url="https://minio.example.com:9000",
    region="us-east-1"
)

# Use the client with upload/download
upload("/local/file.csv", "s3://my-bucket/file.csv", client=client)

docs.title: Streaming Large Files
docs.text:
Process large files in chunks to avoid memory issues:

from file_utils import open_any

# Read a large file in chunks
chunk_size = 1024 * 1024  # 1MB chunks

with open_any("s3://my-bucket/large-file.parquet", "rb") as f:
    while True:
        chunk = f.read(chunk_size)
        if not chunk:
            break
        # Process chunk
        process_chunk(chunk)
